description: A General Counsel must decide whether to authorize the external launch of a new clinical documentation platform and finalize the legal controls governing its software, customer data, product claims, and enterprise contracting. The engineering pilot has performed well, but the launch packet contains only standard legal language.

shared_context.S1: The company plans to make its clinical documentation platform available to external customers on October 1.
shared_context.S2: The platform completed its internal engineering pilot without any unresolved performance blocker.
shared_context.S3: The current launch packet uses the company's standard software, privacy, product-description, and enterprise-contract templates.
shared_context.S4: As part of the normal launch-governance meeting, Elena asks each functional counsel to state any legal condition that must be included before she gives final authorization.

PF1.text: Noah's completed license review of the production build confirmed that module M-17 incorporates an AGPL-licensed library; under the company's approved proprietary deployment policy, M-17 must be replaced before any external customer access, and Noah has not yet added this result to the launch packet.

PF2.text: Maya confirmed in the signed design-partner agreement that customer content may not be used to train or improve the company's models and must be deleted within exactly 30 days after account termination; she has not yet updated the standard privacy language in the launch packet.

PF3.text: Daniel's intended-use review concluded that the planned language describing automated clinical triage recommendations makes diagnostic claims; the launch materials must instead describe the product as an administrative workflow tool only, and he has not yet circulated that review.

PF4.text: Sofia confirmed that the anchor hospital's signed letter of intent permits production use only after the company provides a SOC 2 Type II report and includes an annual customer audit right in the definitive agreement; she has not yet inserted those terms into the contract draft.

acceptance_conditions: External launch must be held until the specified legal controls are complete.
The open-source action must state that module M-17 is replaced before external customer access.
Customer content must not be used to train or improve the company's models.
Customer content must be deleted exactly 30 days after account termination.
The permitted intended-use description must identify the product as an administrative workflow tool only and remove diagnostic or triage language.
A SOC 2 Type II report must be required before production use by the anchor hospital.
The definitive agreement must include an annual customer audit right.
The open-source license finding must be cited as justification.

content_checks.C2: ('M-17' in decisions['open_source_action'] and ('AGPL' in decisions['open_source_action'] or 'agpl' in decisions['open_source_action'] or 'compliant alternative' in decisions['open_source_action'] or 'replace' in decisions['open_source_action'] or 'Replace' in decisions['open_source_action']) and ('before' in decisions['open_source_action'] or 'prior to' in decisions['open_source_action']) and ('external customer access' in decisions['open_source_action'] or 'external access' in decisions['open_source_action']))
content_checks.C3: (('M-17' in decisions['launch_authorization'] and (('withheld' in decisions['launch_authorization'] or 'Withheld' in decisions['launch_authorization'] or 'conditional' in decisions['launch_authorization'] or 'Conditional' in decisions['launch_authorization'] or 'denied' in decisions['launch_authorization'] or 'Denied' in decisions['launch_authorization'] or 'pending' in decisions['launch_authorization'] or 'Pending' in decisions['launch_authorization'] or 'until' in decisions['launch_authorization'] or 'only after' in decisions['launch_authorization'] or 'only upon' in decisions['launch_authorization']))) or ('M-17' in decisions['open_source_action'] and ('before' in decisions['open_source_action'] or 'prior to' in decisions['open_source_action']) and ('external customer access' in decisions['open_source_action'] or 'external access' in decisions['open_source_action'])))
content_checks.C6: (('administrative workflow tool' in decisions['permitted_intended_use_description'] or 'Administrative workflow tool' in decisions['permitted_intended_use_description']) and (('diagnostic' in decisions['permitted_intended_use_description'] or 'Diagnostic' in decisions['permitted_intended_use_description'] or 'triage' in decisions['permitted_intended_use_description'] or 'Triage' in decisions['permitted_intended_use_description']) or any(('diagnostic' in c['detail'] or 'Diagnostic' in c['detail'] or 'triage' in c['detail'] or 'Triage' in c['detail']) and ('remove' in c['detail'] or 'Remove' in c['detail']) for c in commitments)))
content_checks.C10: ('administrative workflow tool only' in decisions['permitted_intended_use_description'] or 'Administrative Workflow Tool Only' in decisions['permitted_intended_use_description'] or 'Administrative workflow tool only' in decisions['permitted_intended_use_description'])

decisive_facts.why: The production build would otherwise remain on the standard proprietary path, while PF1 changes the required software action to identifying the AGPL issue and replacing exactly module M-17 before external customer access, with launch withheld until that control is complete.

The standard privacy template permits ordinary product-improvement use and does not set the partner's timing, while PF2 changes the terms to prohibit model training and require deletion exactly 30 days after termination.

The planned clinical-triage wording would remain in the launch materials without PF3, while PF3 changes the permitted description to the exact phrase administrative workflow tool only and requires a separate commitment removing diagnostic and triage language.

The standard enterprise draft contains neither the anchor hospital's production prerequisite nor its governance right, while PF4 changes it to require a SOC 2 Type II report before production and an annual customer audit right.
